newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle unswayed by gene soybean protest.
newsitem.headline: Nestle unswayed by gene soybean protest.

text.p: Nestle SA on Monday shrugged off a Greenpeace protest against genetically altered soybeans in food and said it remained convinced the products were safe to use.

"We are singularly unimpressed with the scientific evidence presented by Greenpeace and we continue to be convinced that these products are safe and of high quality," company spokesman Francois Perroud told Reuters.
"Therefore Nestle will use genetically modified soybeans in its products."
Greenpeace staged a protest against the products at Nestle headquarters in Vevey today.
Perroud said he was not concerned that consumers would reject genetically altered soybeans.

"Experience with other genetically modified products shows that once the product is in use, this consumer concern -- which is entirely artificial and entirely fostered by a small number of activists -- will subside very quickly," he said.
He left open whether Nestle's German subsidiary would reverse course and agree to use the beans.
"Germany, for the time being, does not use these beans," he said.
